title: One Wrong Move
tagline: A suspicious device in a crowded area, a bomb suit that buys you time but not certainty, and a design that doesn't match anything in the manual.

wake_up.text: On-call rotation for the regional bomb squad. The pager goes off before your alarm does — a suspicious package report at a transit station downtown.

choices.text: Do a complete equipment check before responding
Respond immediately, gear check on arrival

scene_arrival.text: The station is already evacuated and cordoned off. Local police point you toward an unattended bag near the main platform.

choices.text: Begin the initial assessment

random_moment.text: The setup phase before an approach has its own particular quiet — a little different at every call.

choices.text: The robot's camera feed is unusually clear today
A crowd gathers at the perimeter despite the cordon
The scene is quiet and the team is well coordinated today

robot_assessment.text: The robot's camera gets a clear look at the device inside the bag — wiring and components that don't match any known design in the reference manual.

choices.text: Review the imagery carefully

unfamiliar_device.text: This isn't a design you or anyone on your team has seen before. The safe, standard move is a controlled disruption from a distance — reliable, but it destroys any chance of learning who built this or why. A closer, manual approach in the suit could disarm it intact, with real evidence, but nothing about an unfamiliar device is ever fully predictable.

choices.text: Use controlled disruption from a safe distance
Suit up and approach manually to disarm it intact
Call in a second technician to review the imagery with you first
Extend the evacuation perimeter and take more time to study it remotely

device_outcome_disruption.text: The disruption neutralizes the device cleanly and safely from a distance. Whoever built it, and why, will likely never be known — but every person at that station goes home today.

choices.text: Clear the scene

device_outcome_manual.text: The longest forty minutes of your year, hands steady inside the suit, and it works — the device comes apart intact, exactly as it needed to, and now investigators have something real to work with.

choices.text: Hand the device to investigators

device_outcome_second.text: A second set of eyes on the imagery spots a detail you'd missed — enough to inform a safer, better-planned approach than either of you would have made alone.

choices.text: Proceed with the informed approach

device_outcome_wait.text: The extra time confirms a few key details remotely, at the cost of keeping a busy station closed longer than anyone upstairs is happy about. Careful, and slow, in roughly equal measure.

choices.text: Proceed with a now better-informed plan

afternoon_report.text: The device is neutralized, but the paperwork and evidence handoff to investigators is its own careful process, done right the first time or not at all.

choices.text: Document every detail of the response thoroughly
File a summary report and move on

second_call.text: A second call comes in the same day — far more likely a false alarm based on the description, but every call gets treated the same way until proven otherwise.

choices.text: Run the full protocol exactly as if it were the first call
Run an expedited check given the low-risk description

training_review.text: Back at the unit, this morning's unfamiliar device needs to go into the training materials so the next technician who sees one isn't starting from zero.

choices.text: Write up the full technical details for training
Leave a brief note and let the report speak for itself

end_shift.text: The pager stays quiet for the rest of the day. Somewhere, a station that was evacuated this morning is back to its normal rush hour, with no idea how close a call it actually was.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Textbook Response
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the hardest one. This is the response other technicians study for years.

steady_hand.title: Clean and Careful
steady_hand.blurb: No shortcuts, no unnecessary risks — just precise, disciplined work, call after call.

ordinary_day.title: Another Device Neutralized
ordinary_day.blurb: A tense day, handled professionally. The pager could go off again any minute.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through both calls, but there's nothing left in you. This kind of pressure has a real, cumulative cost.

written_up.title: Procedure Review
written_up.blurb: Something about today's approach is heading into a formal procedure review. Everyone's safe. The process still needs a look.
